hypothesis: storage_from_db and basic_account_from_db re-read the storage layout through the provider's settings RwLock on every call (cached_storage_settings, ~3% of heavy-phase server CPU in base-symbols) although OverlayStateProvider already holds it as is_v2. Branching on the captured flag removes one RwLock read-lock/unlock per SLOAD. Expect ~2-3% off heavy (~1-2% total), light flat.
llm_commentary: Branching on the captured is_v2 flag instead of the per-call cached_storage_settings RwLock (commit 82d480e89f) is neutral on x86 (c8a 5.10→5.11s, c8i 6.79→6.74s, both inside run-to-run spread) but a clear 3.0% win on Graviton (c8g 8.31→8.06s, ranges 8.30-8.32 vs 8.02-8.10). That matches the maxperf result: an uncontended parking_lot read-lock is a couple of atomics, which Zen 5 and Granite Rapids absorb, while Neoverse V2 pays noticeably more per atomic RMW across 10k SLOADs per call. The change is also a one-source-of-truth cleanup (the layout used for reads and trie cursors now comes from one field), so it is worth keeping regardless. Next: exp-address-hash, which drops one global keccak-cache lookup per SLOAD.
